educationalPurpose: Make the failed direct-exchange relationships in the barter example visible.

placement.studentGuide: ### Barter and the double coincidence of wants; after "Imagine that Amina has rice and wants shoes. Luis has shoes but wants cooking oil, not rice. Mei has cooking oil and wants repair work. Amina may need several exchanges before she can obtain the shoes. Each exchange takes time and requires agreement about value." and before "For barter to work directly, each person must want what the other person offers at the same time and in suitable amounts."
placement.educatorGuide: ### Barter and the double coincidence of wants; after "Use three people with mismatched goods and wants. First, let the group attempt direct exchange." and before "Then introduce a commonly accepted medium."
placement.guideAnchor: Place at the BD-V-009 visual marker in each guide; use the Shared Student Guide master for the Educator Guide.
placement.format: Single three-role barter-mismatch illustration; full width.

teachingPoint: Direct barter requires both people in an exchange to want what the other offers; none of these three proposed direct exchanges satisfies both people's wants.
visualPattern: Human educational scene recipe with a reusable triangular barter-mismatch variant of the Tier 3 Process flow pattern in the teaching-page print skeleton.

Mei's has/wants pair at lower right
the three failed attempted-exchange paths clockwise

contentRequirements.source: Detailed visual specification — Accessibility and production handoff

palette: paper or white ground (#F6F6F8 or white)
primary purple (#422C70) for restrained structural frame, labels, and attempted-exchange connectors
body neutral (#25252B) for ordinary text and object outlines
controlled orange (#F7941F) only for a failure interruption or one key mismatch cue
style.typography: IBM Plex Sans only; short left-aligned live labels; learner-facing type at least 12pt.
style.shapeAndLineRules: Keep people, goods, thought bubbles, icons, and labels upright. Use straight or 90° elbow monoline connectors with butt caps, miter joins, and open-chevron arrowheads. Pair each orange cue with a broken connector and cross so colour is not its only meaning.
style.geometry: Flat, print-safe MFB Angular Editorial Illustration using one restrained 13° parallelogram framing or section accent and counter-skewed upright contents.
style.emphasis: Use controlled orange only to focus attention on the failure interruption or one key mismatch cue; crossed marks communicate mismatch rather than danger, prohibition, or judgment.
propsAndIcons: simple repair-work cue such as a hand tool
approved first-party icons only if icons are used

prohibitions: Do not show money, Bitcoin, currency, wallets, payment interfaces, QR codes, prices, balances, successful trade, a solution, or a next step.
Do not imply that barter never works; show only this particular three-person mismatch.
Do not add a final explanatory headline, quantities, currencies, additional example copy, advice, claims of returns or safety, real identities, or personal/payment data.

Do not use gradients, glossy or 3D effects, shadows, gold coins, crypto imagery, generic blockchain symbols, corporate-cartoon proportions, redrawn MFB marks, unrelated background scenes, or decorative clutter.

review.notes: The record preserves the approved Amina, Luis, and Mei names and the complete asset-index scenario stated in the brief.
